paper.title: Cascading Bandits for Large-Scale Recommendation Problems

unmapped: Cascade (click) feedback: user scans an ordered list of K items out of L and clicks on the first attractive one; only items up to the click are observed
Reward is non-linear: f(A,w) = 1 - prod_k (1 - w(a_k))
Attraction probabilities are linear in known item features: wbar(e) = x_e^T theta*, ||x_e||_2 <= 1
settings.definition_quote: we assume that the attraction probability of each item $e$, $\bar{w}(e)$, can be approximated by a linear combination of some known $d$-dimensional feature vector $x_e$ and an unknown $d$-dimensional parameter vector of $\theta^\ast$ ... We first derive a regret bound on CascadeLinUCB, under the assumptions that (1) $\bar{w}(e) = x_e^T \theta^\ast$ for all $e \in E$ and (2) $\| x_e \|_2 \leq 1$ for all $e \in E$.

symbols.sigma_alg: algorithm parameter sigma > 0 (assumed noise std / learning-rate parameter), not the noise level

conditions: wbar(e) = x_e^T theta* exactly for all items e
optimal list unique as a set

source.label: thm:bound
source.quote: Under the above assumptions, for any $\sigma > 0$ and any \[ c \geq \frac{1}{\sigma} \sqrt{d \log ( 1 + \frac{nK}{d \sigma^2} )+ 2 \log ( nK ) } + \|\theta^*\|_2 , \] if we run CascadeLinUCB with parameters $\sigma$ and $c$, then \[ R(n) \leq 2c K \sqrt{ \frac{dn \log [ 1+ \frac{nK}{d\sigma^2} ]}{\log ( 1 + \frac{1}{\sigma^2} )} }+ 1. \]

results.notes: Regret is E[sum_t f(A*,w_t) - f(A_t,w_t)] with A* fixed, i.e. pseudo-regret. Text remarks that with sigma=1 and c = sqrt(d log(1+nK/d) + 2 log(nK)) + eta (eta >= ||theta*||), R(n) = O_tilde(K d sqrt(n)). Bound is independent of number of items L. Cascade feedback mapped to partial_monitoring.
